name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_AMINES_MATCH_LIST_Q01 - Medical and biological applications of amino compounds

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II:

List I (Biologically Active Compound) List II (Characteristic / Application)
A. Adrenaline and Ephedrine I. Antihistaminic drug containing a tertiary amino group
B. Novocain II. Synthetic amino compound used as an anaesthetic in dentistry
C. Benadryl III. Naturally occurring secondary amino compounds used to increase blood pressure
D. Quaternary ammonium salts IV. Used commercially as surfactants

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluate Adrenaline and Ephedrine
Adrenaline and ephedrine are biologically active compounds occurring in nature. Both contain a secondary amino group and are clinically utilized to increase blood pressure.

Step 2: Evaluate Novocain
Novocain is a synthetic amino derivative widely used as a local anaesthetic agent in dental procedures.

Step 3: Evaluate Benadryl
Benadryl (diphenhydramine) is a well-known antihistaminic medicinal compound that structurally incorporates a tertiary amino group.

Step 4: Evaluate Quaternary Ammonium Salts
Quaternary ammonium salts possess a permanently positively charged nitrogen center bonded to four alkyl/aryl groups and function effectively as cationic surfactants.

Step 5: Conclude the Matching Pairs
- Adrenaline and Ephedrine pair with naturally occurring secondary amino compounds used to increase blood pressure.
- Novocain pairs with synthetic amino compound used as an anaesthetic in dentistry.
- Benadryl pairs with antihistaminic drug containing a tertiary amino group.
- Quaternary ammonium salts pair with used commercially as surfactants.
Final Answer: A-(III), B-(II), C-(I), D-(IV).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_AMINES_MATCH_LIST_Q02 - Common names and IUPAC names of amines

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II:

List I (Amine Structure / Common Name) List II (IUPAC Nomenclature)
A. \(\mathrm{CH_3-CH(NH_2)-CH_3}\) (Isopropylamine) I. Hexane-1,6-diamine
B. \(\mathrm{NH_2-CH_2-CH=CH_2}\) (Allylamine) II. Prop-2-en-1-amine
C. \(\mathrm{NH_2-(CH_2)_6-NH_2}\) (Hexamethylenediamine) III. \(N,N\)-Dimethylmethanamine
D. \(\mathrm{(CH_3)_3N}\) (Trimethylamine) IV. Propan-2-amine

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Determine the IUPAC Name of Isopropylamine
In \(\mathrm{CH_3-CH(NH_2)-CH_3}\), the longest continuous carbon chain contains three carbon atoms (propane), and the amino substituent is attached at carbon-2. Dropping the 'e' from propane yields Propan-2-amine.

Step 2: Determine the IUPAC Name of Allylamine
In \(\mathrm{NH_2-CH_2-CH=CH_2}\), the three-carbon chain contains both a double bond and a principal amino functional group. Numbering starts at the carbon bearing the amino group (carbon-1), putting the alkene at carbon-2. The IUPAC name is Prop-2-en-1-amine.

Step 3: Determine the IUPAC Name of Hexamethylenediamine
In \(\mathrm{NH_2-(CH_2)_6-NH_2}\), a six-carbon alkane chain bears two terminal amino groups at carbon-1 and carbon-6. Retaining the final 'e' of hexane gives Hexane-1,6-diamine.

Step 4: Determine the IUPAC Name of Trimethylamine
In \(\mathrm{(CH_3)_3N}\), nitrogen is bonded to three identical methyl groups. The principal chain is methanamine, and the two additional methyl substituents are designated with locant \(N\) as \(N,N\)-Dimethylmethanamine.

Step 5: Conclude the Matching Pairs
- Isopropylamine corresponds to Propan-2-amine.
- Allylamine corresponds to Prop-2-en-1-amine.
- Hexamethylenediamine corresponds to Hexane-1,6-diamine.
- Trimethylamine corresponds to \(N,N\)-Dimethylmethanamine.
Final Answer: A-(IV), B-(II), C-(I), D-(III).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_AMINES_MATCH_LIST_Q03 - Synthetic preparation methods of primary amines

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II:

List I (Synthetic Preparation Method) List II (Distinctive Feature / Principle)
A. Gabriel phthalimide synthesis I. Yields a primary amine possessing one fewer carbon atom than the precursor amide
B. Hoffmann bromamide degradation II. Synthesizes exclusively aliphatic primary amines because aryl halides do not undergo nucleophilic substitution
C. Reduction of alkyl nitriles with \(\mathrm{LiAlH_4}\) III. Achieves ascent of the amine series by introducing an additional carbon atom
D. Reduction of nitrobenzene using \(\mathrm{Fe/HCl}\) IV. Industrially preferred since generated \(\mathrm{FeCl_2}\) hydrolyses to release \(\mathrm{HCl}\), requiring minimal acid

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluate Gabriel Phthalimide Synthesis
Phthalimide is deprotonated by potassium hydroxide to generate the phthalimide anion, which acts as a nucleophile with alkyl halides. However, aryl halides do not undergo nucleophilic substitution with this bulky anion due to partial double bond character and resonance stabilization. Therefore, this reaction is restricted purely to aliphatic primary amines.

Step 2: Evaluate Hoffmann Bromamide Degradation
Treatment of an amide with bromine and sodium hydroxide triggers intramolecular migration of an alkyl or aryl group from carbonyl carbon to nitrogen, accompanied by loss of the carbonyl group as carbonate. The produced primary amine contains exactly one carbon atom less than the parent amide.

Step 3: Evaluate Reduction of Nitriles
Reduction of nitriles (\(\mathrm{R-C\equiv N}\)) with lithium aluminium hydride converts the cyano carbon into a methylene group (\(\mathrm{R-CH_2-NH_2}\)). This reaction is conventionally employed for the ascent of the amine series, yielding an amine with one more carbon than the starting alkyl halide from which the nitrile was formed.

Step 4: Evaluate Reduction of Nitrobenzene with Iron Scrap and Hydrochloric Acid
Reduction of nitro compounds using iron scrap and hydrochloric acid is favored because the ferrous chloride (\(\mathrm{FeCl_2}\)) formed during the reaction undergoes hydrolysis by water to regenerate hydrochloric acid. Thus, only a catalytic or initiator amount of hydrochloric acid is required.

Step 5: Conclude the Matching Pairs
- Gabriel phthalimide synthesis matches with synthesizes exclusively aliphatic primary amines because aryl halides do not undergo nucleophilic substitution.
- Hoffmann bromamide degradation matches with yields a primary amine possessing one fewer carbon atom than the precursor amide.
- Reduction of alkyl nitriles matches with achieves ascent of the amine series by introducing an additional carbon atom.
- Reduction of nitrobenzene using \(\mathrm{Fe/HCl}\) matches with industrially preferred since generated \(\mathrm{FeCl_2}\) hydrolyses to release \(\mathrm{HCl}\), requiring minimal acid.
Final Answer: A-(II), B-(I), C-(III), D-(IV).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_AMINES_MATCH_LIST_Q04 - Chemical tests and distinguishing reactions of amines

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II:

List I (Reaction / Chemical Test) List II (Characteristic Observation / Behavior)
A. Heating primary amine with \(\mathrm{CHCl_3}\) and ethanolic \(\mathrm{KOH}\) I. Forms an \(N,N\)-dialkylsulphonamide that lacks an acidic hydrogen and is insoluble in alkali
B. Reaction of primary amine with benzenesulphonyl chloride II. Liberates an extremely foul-smelling isocyanide (carbylamine)
C. Reaction of secondary amine with benzenesulphonyl chloride III. Liberates nitrogen gas quantitatively alongside alcohol formation
D. Reaction of primary aliphatic amine with nitrous acid IV. Forms an \(N\)-alkylsulphonamide possessing an acidic hydrogen on nitrogen, dissolving readily in aqueous alkali

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluate the Carbylamine Reaction
Both aliphatic and aromatic primary amines react with chloroform and ethanolic potassium hydroxide upon heating to synthesize isocyanides (carbylamines), which are characterized by an intensely intolerable, foul odour. Secondary and tertiary amines do not exhibit this transformation.

Step 2: Evaluate the Hinsberg Reaction with Primary Amines
Benzenesulphonyl chloride reacts with a primary amine to form an \(N\)-alkylbenzenesulphonamide. The hydrogen atom directly bound to nitrogen in this sulphonamide is strongly acidic due to the strong electron-withdrawing nature of the adjacent sulphonyl group; consequently, it dissolves in aqueous potassium hydroxide or sodium hydroxide.

Step 3: Evaluate the Hinsberg Reaction with Secondary Amines
Reaction with a secondary amine produces an \(N,N\)-dialkylbenzenesulphonamide. Because there is no hydrogen atom attached to the nitrogen atom in this product, it lacks acidic character and remains insoluble in aqueous alkali.

Step 4: Evaluate the Reaction of Primary Aliphatic Amines with Nitrous Acid
Primary aliphatic amines react with nitrous acid (prepared in situ from \(\mathrm{NaNO_2 + HCl}\)) to form highly unstable alkyldiazonium salts. These decompose instantaneously to release nitrogen gas quantitatively, forming alcohols and carbocation rearrangement products.

Step 5: Conclude the Matching Pairs
- Heating primary amine with chloroform and ethanolic potassium hydroxide corresponds to liberating an extremely foul-smelling isocyanide.
- Reaction of primary amine with benzenesulphonyl chloride corresponds to forming an \(N\)-alkylsulphonamide possessing an acidic hydrogen that dissolves readily in aqueous alkali.
- Reaction of secondary amine with benzenesulphonyl chloride corresponds to forming an \(N,N\)-dialkylsulphonamide lacking an acidic hydrogen that is insoluble in alkali.
- Reaction of primary aliphatic amine with nitrous acid corresponds to liberating nitrogen gas quantitatively alongside alcohol formation.
Final Answer: A-(II), B-(IV), C-(I), D-(III).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_AMINES_MATCH_LIST_Q05 - Electrophilic aromatic substitution reactions of aniline

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II:

List I (Reaction Conditions on Aniline) List II (Principal Product / Observation)
A. Treatment with bromine water at room temperature I. Selective formation of \(p\)-nitroaniline as the major product
B. Direct nitration with conc. \(\mathrm{HNO_3 + H_2SO_4}\) at \(288\text{ K}\) II. Substantial formation of \(m\)-nitroaniline (\(47\%\)) alongside ortho and para isomers
C. Acetylation with \(\mathrm{(CH_3CO)_2O}\) followed by nitration and hydrolysis III. Immediate formation of a white precipitate of 2,4,6-tribromoaniline
D. Heating with concentrated \(\mathrm{H_2SO_4}\) at \(453\text{--}473\text{ K}\) IV. Sulphanilic acid which exists as a dipolar zwitterion

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluate Bromination of Aniline with Bromine Water
The amino group (\(-\mathrm{NH_2}\)) is an exceptionally powerful activating group that strongly increases electron density at ortho and para positions via resonance. Reaction of aniline with bromine water proceeds without catalyst to substitute all three positions simultaneously, giving an immediate white precipitate of 2,4,6-tribromoaniline.

Step 2: Evaluate Direct Nitration of Aniline
In the strongly acidic nitrating mixture (\(\mathrm{HNO_3 + H_2SO_4}\)), aniline is extensively protonated into anilinium ion (\(-\mathrm{NH_3^+}\)). Because the anilinium ion is strongly deactivating and meta-directing, direct nitration yields \(47\%\) \(m\)-nitroaniline, \(51\%\) \(p\)-nitroaniline, and \(2\%\) \(o\)-nitroaniline.

Step 3: Evaluate Controlled Nitration via Protection
To avoid polysubstitution, tarry oxidation products, and meta-substitution, the amino group is protected by acetylation with acetic anhydride to form acetanilide (\(-\mathrm{NHCOCH_3}\)). In acetanilide, the nitrogen lone pair is delocalized onto the carbonyl oxygen, reducing activation. Subsequent nitration followed by acid or alkaline hydrolysis affords \(p\)-nitroaniline cleanly as the major product.

Step 4: Evaluate Sulphonation of Aniline
Aniline reacts with concentrated sulphuric acid to form anilinium hydrogensulphate, which upon sustained heating at \(453\text{--}473\text{ K}\) undergoes rearrangement to yield \(p\)-aminobenzenesulphonic acid (sulphanilic acid). The acidic sulphonic group transfers a proton to the basic amino group, causing sulphanilic acid to exist primarily as a dipolar zwitterion (\(\mathrm{H_3N^+-C_6H_4-SO_3^-}\)).

Step 5: Conclude the Matching Pairs
- Treatment with bromine water matches with immediate formation of a white precipitate of 2,4,6-tribromoaniline.
- Direct nitration matches with substantial formation of \(m\)-nitroaniline (\(47\%\)) alongside ortho and para isomers.
- Acetylation followed by nitration and hydrolysis matches with selective formation of \(p\)-nitroaniline as the major product.
- Heating with concentrated \(\mathrm{H_2SO_4}\) at \(453\text{--}473\text{ K}\) matches with sulphanilic acid which exists as a dipolar zwitterion.
Final Answer: A-(III), B-(II), C-(I), D-(IV).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_AMINES_MATCH_LIST_Q06 - Nitrogen displacement reactions of benzenediazonium chloride

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II:

List I (Reagent Reacting with \(\mathrm{C_6H_5N_2^+Cl^-}\)) List II (Aromatic Product Formed)
A. \(\mathrm{Cu_2Cl_2 / HCl}\) I. Fluorobenzene (\(\mathrm{C_6H_5F}\))
B. \(\mathrm{KI}\) (aqueous solution) II. Chlorobenzene (\(\mathrm{C_6H_5Cl}\))
C. \(\mathrm{HBF_4}\) followed by heating (\(\Delta\)) III. Benzene (\(\mathrm{C_6H_6}\))
D. \(\mathrm{H_3PO_2 + H_2O}\) IV. Iodobenzene (\(\mathrm{C_6H_5I}\))

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluate Reaction with \(\mathrm{Cu_2Cl_2 / HCl}\)
When benzenediazonium chloride is treated with cuprous chloride dissolved in hydrochloric acid, the diazonium group is replaced by a chloride ion via the Sandmeyer reaction, yielding chlorobenzene (\(\mathrm{C_6H_5Cl}\)) and liberating nitrogen gas.

Step 2: Evaluate Reaction with Aqueous Potassium Iodide
Iodide ion is sufficiently nucleophilic and easily oxidizable, so no copper catalyst is required. Shaking or warming the diazonium salt solution with potassium iodide cleanly produces iodobenzene (\(\mathrm{C_6H_5I}\)).

Step 3: Evaluate Reaction with \(\mathrm{HBF_4}\) Followed by Heating
Treatment of benzenediazonium chloride with fluoroboric acid precipitates benzenediazonium fluoroborate (\(\mathrm{C_6H_5N_2^+BF_4^-}\)). When isolated dry and heated, it undergoes thermal decomposition (Balz–Schiemann reaction) to yield fluorobenzene (\(\mathrm{C_6H_5F}\)), \(\mathrm{BF_3}\), and nitrogen gas.

Step 4: Evaluate Reaction with Hypophosphorous Acid
Mild reducing agents like hypophosphorous acid (phosphinic acid, \(\mathrm{H_3PO_2}\)) reduce arenediazonium salts to parent arenes (benzene, \(\mathrm{C_6H_6}\)) while being oxidised to phosphorous acid (\(\mathrm{H_3PO_3}\)).

Step 5: Conclude the Matching Pairs
- \(\mathrm{Cu_2Cl_2 / HCl}\) yields Chlorobenzene.
- \(\mathrm{KI}\) yields Iodobenzene.
- \(\mathrm{HBF_4}\) followed by heating yields Fluorobenzene.
- \(\mathrm{H_3PO_2 + H_2O}\) yields Benzene.
Final Answer: A-(II), B-(IV), C-(I), D-(III).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_AMINES_MATCH_LIST_Q07 - Coupling and substitution reactions of arenediazonium salts

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II:

List I (Reaction Scheme) List II (Product and Characteristic)
A. \(\mathrm{C_6H_5N_2^+Cl^-} + \text{Phenol} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{OH^-}}\) I. Phenol with liberation of \(\mathrm{N_2}\) and \(\mathrm{HCl}\)
B. \(\mathrm{C_6H_5N_2^+Cl^-} + \text{Aniline} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{H^+}}\) II. Nitrobenzene via copper-catalysed nitro replacement
C. \(\mathrm{C_6H_5N_2^+Cl^-} + \mathrm{H_2O} \xrightarrow{283\text{ K}}\) III. \(p\)-Hydroxyazobenzene (orange dye)
D. \(\mathrm{C_6H_5N_2^+BF_4^-} + \mathrm{NaNO_2(aq)} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{Cu, \Delta}}\) IV. \(p\)-Aminoazobenzene (yellow dye)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluate Coupling with Phenol in Alkaline Medium
In mildly alkaline conditions (pH 9-10), phenol is converted to phenoxide ion, which strongly activates the para position towards electrophilic aromatic attack by the benzenediazonium cation. Coupling takes place at the para position to form \(p\)-hydroxyazobenzene, which is an orange azo dye.

Step 2: Evaluate Coupling with Aniline in Mildly Acidic Medium
In mildly acidic medium (pH 4-5), aniline couples at its para position with benzenediazonium chloride via electrophilic aromatic substitution, giving \(p\)-aminoazobenzene, which is a yellow azo dye.

Step 3: Evaluate Hydrolysis of Diazonium Salt
When an aqueous solution of benzenediazonium chloride is allowed to warm up to \(283\text{ K}\), the diazonium group undergoes nucleophilic displacement by water to produce phenol along with the quantitative evolution of nitrogen gas and hydrochloric acid.

Step 4: Evaluate Replacement by Nitro Group
When benzenediazonium fluoroborate is heated with an aqueous solution of sodium nitrite in the presence of copper powder catalyst, the diazo moiety is replaced by the nitro group, forming nitrobenzene.

Step 5: Conclude the Matching Pairs
- Reaction with phenol in basic medium produces \(p\)-hydroxyazobenzene (orange dye).
- Reaction with aniline in acidic medium produces \(p\)-aminoazobenzene (yellow dye).
- Reaction with water at \(283\text{ K}\) produces phenol with liberation of \(\mathrm{N_2}\) and \(\mathrm{HCl}\).
- Reaction of fluoroborate with aqueous sodium nitrite and copper produces nitrobenzene.
Final Answer: A-(III), B-(IV), C-(I), D-(II).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_AMINES_MATCH_LIST_Q08 - Basicity trends and electronic factors in amines

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II:

List I (Basicity System / Comparison) List II (Observed Order / Governing Principle)
A. Aqueous basicity order of ethyl-substituted amines I. \((\mathrm{CH_3})_2\mathrm{NH} > \mathrm{CH_3NH_2} > (\mathrm{CH_3})_3\mathrm{N} > \mathrm{NH_3}\) due to minimal steric hindrance with hydration
B. Aqueous basicity order of methyl-substituted amines II. \((\mathrm{C_2H_5})_2\mathrm{NH} > (\mathrm{C_2H_5})_3\mathrm{N} > \mathrm{C_2H_5NH_2} > \mathrm{NH_3}\) resulting from bulky ethyl groups hindering cation solvation
C. Basicity order of simple alkylamines in the gaseous phase III. \(\text{Tertiary} > \text{Secondary} > \text{Primary} > \mathrm{NH_3}\) governed entirely by inductive (\(+\mathrm{I}\)) electron release
D. Basic strength comparison of aniline relative to ammonia IV. Markedly weaker base because the nitrogen lone pair participates in five conjugative resonance contributors

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Analyze the Basicity of Ethyl-Substituted Amines in Aqueous Solution
In aqueous solution, the basicity of alkylamines depends on a delicate interplay between the electron-releasing inductive effect (\(+\mathrm{I}\)), stabilization of the conjugate cation by hydration/solvation, and steric hindrance. For ethyl groups, the greater size creates steric resistance to hydration in the triethylammonium ion, making diethylamine a stronger base than triethylamine. The overall sequence is \((\mathrm{C_2H_5})_2\mathrm{NH} > (\mathrm{C_2H_5})_3\mathrm{N} > \mathrm{C_2H_5NH_2} > \mathrm{NH_3}\).

Step 2: Analyze the Basicity of Methyl-Substituted Amines in Aqueous Solution
Because the methyl group is small, steric hindrance to hydration is minimal. However, the trimethylammonium cation has only one hydrogen available for hydrogen bonding with water molecules, drastically decreasing its solvation stability compared to methylammonium and dimethylammonium ions. Consequently, the observed basicity follows \((\mathrm{CH_3})_2\mathrm{NH} > \mathrm{CH_3NH_2} > (\mathrm{CH_3})_3\mathrm{N} > \mathrm{NH_3}\).

Step 3: Analyze the Basicity of Alkylamines in the Gaseous Phase
In the gas phase, no solvent molecules are present to provide hydration stabilization. Hence, basicity is governed purely by the electron-donating inductive effect (\(+\mathrm{I}\)) of alkyl groups, which disperses the positive charge of the protonated amine. The order follows strictly: \(\text{Tertiary} > \text{Secondary} > \text{Primary} > \mathrm{NH_3}\).

Step 4: Analyze the Relative Basicity of Aniline Versus Ammonia
In aniline, the unshared electron pair on nitrogen is in direct resonance with the aromatic ring, giving five resonating structures. Protonation yields the anilinium ion, which has only two Kekule resonating structures. Because aniline is stabilized to a greater extent by resonance than the anilinium cation, proton acceptance is unfavorable, rendering aniline a far weaker base than ammonia.

Step 5: Conclude the Matching Pairs
- Aqueous basicity of ethyl-substituted amines matches with \((\mathrm{C_2H_5})_2\mathrm{NH} > (\mathrm{C_2H_5})_3\mathrm{N} > \mathrm{C_2H_5NH_2} > \mathrm{NH_3}\).
- Aqueous basicity of methyl-substituted amines matches with \((\mathrm{CH_3})_2\mathrm{NH} > \mathrm{CH_3NH_2} > (\mathrm{CH_3})_3\mathrm{N} > \mathrm{NH_3}\).
- Gaseous phase basicity matches with \(\text{Tertiary} > \text{Secondary} > \text{Primary} > \mathrm{NH_3}\).
- Aniline basic strength relative to ammonia matches with markedly weaker base because the nitrogen lone pair participates in five conjugative resonance contributors.
Final Answer: A-(II), B-(I), C-(III), D-(IV).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_AMINES_MATCH_LIST_Q09 - Multistep reaction sequences involving amines and diazonium salts

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II:

List I (Multistep Reaction Sequence) List II (Final Major Organic Product)
A. \(\mathrm{CH_3CH_2Cl} \xrightarrow{\text{ethanolic NaCN}} \mathrm{X} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{H_2 / Ni}} \mathrm{Y}\) I. Phenol
B. \(\mathrm{C_6H_5NO_2} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{Fe/HCl}} \mathrm{X} \xrightarrow[273\text{--}278\text{ K}]{\mathrm{NaNO_2 + HCl}} \mathrm{Y} \xrightarrow[\Delta]{\mathrm{H_2O / H^+}} \mathrm{Z}\) II. Propan-1-amine
C. \(\mathrm{C_6H_5CONH_2} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{Br_2 + 4NaOH}} \mathrm{X}\) III. Aniline
D. \(\mathrm{C_6H_5NH_2} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{Br_2(aq)}} \mathrm{X} \xrightarrow[273\text{--}278\text{ K}]{\mathrm{NaNO_2 + HCl}} \mathrm{Y} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{H_3PO_2 / H_2O}} \mathrm{Z}\) IV. 1,3,5-Tribromobenzene

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Trace Sequence A
Treatment of chloroethane (\(\mathrm{CH_3CH_2Cl}\)) with ethanolic sodium cyanide replaces chlorine by cyanide to yield propanenitrile (\(\mathrm{CH_3CH_2CN}\)) as compound \(\mathrm{X}\). Catalytic hydrogenation of propanenitrile with \(\mathrm{H_2/Ni}\) reduces the nitrile group to a primary amine, producing propan-1-amine (\(\mathrm{CH_3CH_2CH_2NH_2}\)).

Step 2: Trace Sequence B
Reduction of nitrobenzene (\(\mathrm{C_6H_5NO_2}\)) with \(\mathrm{Fe/HCl}\) gives aniline (\(\mathrm{C_6H_5NH_2}\)) as intermediate \(\mathrm{X}\). Diazotisation of aniline with \(\mathrm{NaNO_2 + HCl}\) at \(273\text{--}278\text{ K}\) affords benzenediazonium chloride (\(\mathrm{C_6H_5N_2^+Cl^-}\)) as intermediate \(\mathrm{Y}\). Warming the diazonium salt solution with acidic water results in hydrolysis, yielding phenol (\(\mathrm{C_6H_5OH}\)) as product \(\mathrm{Z}\).

Step 3: Trace Sequence C
Treatment of benzamide (\(\mathrm{C_6H_5CONH_2}\)) with bromine and aqueous sodium hydroxide undergoes Hoffmann bromamide degradation. The carbonyl group is removed as carbonate, yielding the aromatic primary amine aniline (\(\mathrm{C_6H_5NH_2}\)).

Step 4: Trace Sequence D
Reaction of aniline with aqueous bromine gives 2,4,6-tribromoaniline as intermediate \(\mathrm{X}\). Subsequent diazotisation at \(273\text{--}278\text{ K}\) converts the amino group into the diazonium salt 2,4,6-tribromobenzenediazonium chloride (\(\mathrm{Y}\)). Deamination using hypophosphorous acid (\(\mathrm{H_3PO_2}\)) replaces the diazo group with hydrogen, cleanly yielding 1,3,5-tribromobenzene (\(\mathrm{Z}\)).

Step 5: Conclude the Matching Pairs
- Sequence A yields Propan-1-amine.
- Sequence B yields Phenol.
- Sequence C yields Aniline.
- Sequence D yields 1,3,5-Tribromobenzene.
Final Answer: A-(II), B-(I), C-(III), D-(IV).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_AMINES_MATCH_LIST_Q10 - Structural properties and anomalous behavior of amines

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II:

List I (Observed Phenomenon) List II (Governing Cause / Mechanism)
A. \(\mathrm{C-N-C}\) bond angle in trimethylamine is \(108^\circ\) instead of tetrahedral \(109.5^\circ\) I. Progressive decrease in hydrogen atoms on nitrogen reduces the extent of intermolecular hydrogen bonding
B. Boiling point trend: \(\text{Butan-1-amine } (350.8\text{ K}) > \text{Diethylamine } (329.3\text{ K}) > N,N\text{-Dimethylethanamine } (310.5\text{ K})\) II. Unshared electron pair exerts greater repulsion than bonding pairs, compressing the pyramidal geometry
C. Decreasing solubility in water as the hydrocarbon part of amines increases in size III. Growth of the hydrophobic non-polar hydrocarbon chain resists interaction with polar water molecules
D. Aniline does not undergo Friedel–Crafts alkylation or acylation IV. Lewis acid catalyst \(\mathrm{AlCl_3}\) coordinates to the lone pair of nitrogen, generating a strongly deactivating positive charge

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluate the Bond Angle in Trimethylamine
The nitrogen atom in trimethylamine is \(sp^3\) hybridised with a pyramidal geometry. Three orbitals overlap with carbon orbitals, while the fourth orbital accommodates an unshared electron pair. Repulsion between the lone pair and bonding pairs compresses the \(\mathrm{C-N-C}\) angle from the regular tetrahedral angle (\(109.5^\circ\)) to \(108^\circ\).

Step 2: Evaluate the Boiling Point Trend of Isomeric Amines
In primary amines (butan-1-amine), nitrogen possesses two hydrogen atoms available for extensive intermolecular hydrogen bonding. In secondary amines (diethylamine), only one hydrogen atom is available, leading to moderate association. Tertiary amines (\(N,N\)-dimethylethanamine) possess no hydrogen attached to nitrogen and cannot form intermolecular hydrogen bonds among themselves, resulting in the lowest boiling point.

Step 3: Evaluate the Solubility Pattern in Water
Lower aliphatic amines dissolve readily in water because they form intermolecular hydrogen bonds with water molecules. As molar mass increases, the alkyl group expands in size. The non-polar alkyl chain is hydrophobic, opposing solvation and ultimately causing higher amines to become essentially insoluble in water.

Step 4: Evaluate the Failure of Friedel–Crafts Reaction on Aniline
Friedel–Crafts reactions require anhydrous aluminium chloride (\(\mathrm{AlCl_3}\)) as a Lewis acid catalyst. Aniline is a Lewis base; its nitrogen lone pair donates electrons to \(\mathrm{AlCl_3}\) to form an unreactive adduct or complex salt (\(\mathrm{C_6H_5-NH_2^+-AlCl_3^-}\)). This places a formal positive charge on nitrogen, converting the strongly activating amino group into a strongly deactivating meta-directing center that completely inhibits electrophilic attack.

Step 5: Conclude the Matching Pairs
- Trimethylamine bond angle of \(108^\circ\) matches with unshared electron pair exerts greater repulsion than bonding pairs, compressing the pyramidal geometry.
- Boiling point trend of isomeric amines matches with progressive decrease in hydrogen atoms on nitrogen reduces the extent of intermolecular hydrogen bonding.
- Decreasing solubility with molar mass matches with growth of the hydrophobic non-polar hydrocarbon chain resists interaction with polar water molecules.
- Failure of Friedel-Crafts reaction on aniline matches with Lewis acid catalyst \(\mathrm{AlCl_3}\) coordinates to the lone pair of nitrogen, generating a strongly deactivating positive charge.
Final Answer: A-(II), B-(I), C-(III), D-(IV).
